use_cases.name: Launch day
use_cases.title: Blowhorn for launch day
use_cases.headline: Make the first hour count.
use_cases.lead: Schedule the announcement and its amplifications ahead of time. Every profile you run joins the same sound wave at the moment you pick.
use_cases.description: Plan a product launch so the announcement goes out everywhere at the right moment, and every profile you add amplifies it in the first hour.

art.alt: Major Blowhorn, a teal rooster drill sergeant in a campaign hat, pointing and shouting through his gold bullhorn, Caribbean Green sound waves pouring out of it

pains.b: The announcement goes out, then you chase people in Slack while the moment passes.
Personal, company and project profiles, each in its own composer, for every network.

pains.t: The schedule lives on one laptop
pains.b: Close that lid and the wave waits. A meeting or a flight should not kill the launch.

gets.b: Schedule the launch post and its reposts, quotes and reactions ahead of time.
Every profile you run joins the same sound wave at the moment you pick, each posting as itself.
Coordinated so the same post isn't sent from two computers. One command pauses the whole wave.
Run history and analytics from every computer in one place. Analytics cover LinkedIn, X and Bluesky.

use_cases.prompt: Queue the launch post for Tuesday 9:00, have every profile amplify it, then --dry-run the whole wave.
use_cases.major: Sound the horn at oh-nine-hundred. Every profile, one wave.

faq.q: Does a computer have to be awake?
faq.a: One set up for the profile does. Install Blowhorn on as many computers as you like; as long as one of them is awake, it covers the schedule. The queue lives in your Blowhorn account.
LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Hacker News: Blowhorn types in your own browser, signed in as you. Slack, Bluesky and GitHub go through their APIs. The desktop app and the Python CLI share the same queue.

faq.q: Will the same post go out twice?
faq.a: Your computers coordinate through one queue, so the same post isn't sent from two of them.

use_cases.name: Open source release
use_cases.title: Blowhorn for open source releases
use_cases.headline: Ship the tag. Tell every channel, as you.
use_cases.lead: Announce a release on Slack, Hacker News, Reddit, LinkedIn, X and Bluesky, and rally reactions on the GitHub issue, from one queue, as you.
use_cases.description: Announce a release or project milestone on Slack, Hacker News, Reddit, LinkedIn, X and Bluesky, and rally GitHub reactions, from one queue, as yourself.

art.alt: Trench Trooper, a muddy pig in a helmet holding a rifle with a teal tab bayonet and a gold periscope

pains.b: None of the schedulers we checked support Hacker News, and most skip GitHub and Slack.
Everyone means to share the release. Few remember in the first hour.
Developers notice votes, blast posts and bot-branded messages.

gets.b: GitHub reactions, Slack as you, Hacker News submit and comment, plus LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Bluesky, from one queue.
Queue the release from every profile you run, each posting as itself. Team invites are coming soon.

gets.t: Slack as you, no bot to invite
gets.b: Sends as you through Slack's API, using your Slack session linked through the Blowhorn extension or a Slack token you add. Either one is kept in your Blowhorn account.
Types key by key in your own browser for LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Hacker News. Caps itself. CAPTCHA and 2FA stay with you.

use_cases.prompt: Draft the release posts from CHANGELOG.md, react on the GitHub issue, submit to Hacker News, then --dry-run the rest.
use_cases.major: A release without a roll call is a secret. Sound off.

faq.q: Does it vote on Hacker News?
faq.a: Never. It submits stories and comments, nothing else. Link submissions are capped at 2 per profile per day.

faq.q: Does Blowhorn install a Slack app?
faq.a: No. Blowhorn works on Slack through Slack's API, never the browser, and sends as you with your Slack session, linked through the Blowhorn extension, or a Slack token you add. Either one is kept in your Blowhorn account.
Each computer that acts needs macOS 13 or newer today. Windows and Linux: not today. The queue lives in your Blowhorn account.

use_cases.name: Conference
use_cases.title: Blowhorn for conferences
use_cases.headline: Queue the week. Walk the floor.
use_cases.lead: Queue the pre-event, day-of and follow-up posts once. As long as one of your computers set up for that profile is awake, it covers the schedule while you're at the booth.
use_cases.description: Promote a talk, booth or meetup before, during and after the event, from one queue, while any awake computer covers the schedule.

art.alt: Sleeper Cell, a black-faced sheep in a watch cap, teal monocle and coral scarf, crouched behind a padlock shield with a radar cloaker

pains.t: The schedule is in your bag
pains.b: The talk post is queued on the laptop you closed when you left for the venue.
Everyone meant to post. The session started anyway.
Sending a comment or reply means another composer for LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Hacker News, while you're on the floor.

gets.b: Pre-event, day-of and follow-up posts in one queue, on any awake computer set up for the profile.
Queue the week from every profile you run, each posting as itself. Team invites are coming soon.
Every brand and project profile you run, from one menu bar app.
Send comments and replies from the same queue you posted from. LinkedIn, X, Reddit and Hacker News run in your own browser.

use_cases.prompt: Queue pre-event, day-of and follow-up posts for the talk, then --dry-run.
use_cases.major: The floor is yours. The queue holds the line.

faq.q: What if my laptop is closed?
faq.a: As long as one of your computers is awake and set up for that profile, it covers the schedule. The queue lives in your Blowhorn account; your account never posts.

faq.q: Can speakers join from their own laptops?
faq.a: You can install Blowhorn on as many of your own computers as you like. Speakers and teammates joining your account with their own profiles is coming soon.

faq.q: Windows or Linux at the booth?
faq.a: Not today. Blowhorn runs on macOS 13 or newer, as the desktop app or the Python CLI.
